verdict.rationale: Stripe Identity documents creating a VerificationSession via the API, tracking its status through the lifecycle with status-change events, and retrieving verification results and collected images programmatically with a secret key. Nothing in the evidence covers cancelling or redacting a session through the API, so the lifecycle as written is only partly documented. Missing for 10: documented cancel endpoint, documented redact endpoint, independent hands-on corroboration of end-to-end API lifecycle control.

support.subject: As a developer, the whole verification lifecycle is drivable through the API — create a session, get its status, retrieve results and captured media, and cancel or redact it — with every step documented

citations.quote: This API tracks a verification, from initial creation through the entire verification process, and shows verification results upon completion.
Stripe generates events every time a session changes status.
You can access most verification details programmatically... using your secret key.
You might need to access the sensitive verification results, such as your user’s date of birth or pictures of the collected document, at a later date.
